recalibration_criteria.description: Criteria for determining which Moderate (DifficultyScore=3) items warrant recalibration to Difficult (DifficultyScore=4). These criteria are ordered by diagnostic weight — an item meeting criteria 1 AND (2 OR 3) is a strong candidate. An item meeting only criterion 7 (e.g., long EC text on a definition-match item) is NOT a candidate.

must_have.criterion: CalculationItem is true AND requires 3+ distinct arithmetic operations
must_have.rationale: Multi-step calculations are the clearest driver of genuine difficulty. Items requiring chained arithmetic (e.g., learning curve → cumulative average → total labor hours) test procedural mastery and working memory — hallmarks of CMA Difficult items. Pack B benchmark: all 3 sampled Difficult items (P1B-A-083, P1B-B-119, P1B-B-200) have DifficultyScore=4, CognitiveLevel=Apply, and require 3+ calculation steps.
examples_from_benchmark: P1B-B-119: 4th-unit learning curve time = 100 × 4^(-0.32193) = 64 — requires understanding of the learning curve exponent, proper substitution, and logarithmic application
P1B-B-200: 8-unit cumulative average = 1,000 × 0.9³ = 729 × 8 = 5,832 total hours — requires chaining cumulative averages across 3 doublings
must_have.pack_b_difficult_distribution: 29 Difficult items in Pack B, 25 of 29 (86%) are in Sections B and C. Pack B Difficult items cluster in calculation-heavy micro-topics: learning curves, cash budget with borrowing constraints, direct materials purchases, variance reconciliation.

must_have.criterion: CognitiveLevel is Apply AND Section is A, B, C, or D
must_have.rationale: Apply is the minimum cognitive level for Difficult-caliber items in calculation domains. Remember/Understand items — even in Sections A-D — are predominantly recognition tasks that do not warrant Difficult. Agent F's S810.1 analysis confirmed: zero of 38 Domain E/D seeds scored above Apply, and zero justified Difficult. The Bloom's→Difficulty bridge is: Apply → Moderate(3) or Difficult(4); Analyze → Difficult(4) or Very Difficult(5); Evaluate → Very Difficult(5).
must_have.section_exclusion: Sections E and F are excluded from the upward recalibration pool. Agent F's matrix showed 23 of 38 Domain E seeds (60.5%) are OVERSTATED — the current Difficult-labeled items are inflated. Sections E/F items should be recalibrated DOWNWARD (Moderate→Easy/Moderate-Easy per DL-031), not upward. This reallocates the ~464 surplus Moderate count toward the downward direction for conceptual domains.
must_have.cognitive_constraint: Only 5 items pool-wide have CognitiveLevel=Analyze; zero have Evaluate. This severely limits the pool of items that can defensibly reach Difficult(4) or Very Difficult(5) at this time.

must_have.criterion: Tests subtle conceptual distinctions or framework comparisons
must_have.rationale: Items that require distinguishing between similar-but-opposite concepts (e.g., principal vs. agent under ASC 606, operating vs. finance lease criteria, net present value vs. internal rate of return decision rules) test higher-order understanding. These are frequently missed on the CMA exam and warrant Difficult labeling even without multi-step calculation.
must_have.examples: P1B-A-083: principal vs. agent analysis under ASC 606 — requires parsing whether the entity controls goods before transfer. Distractors test gross-vs-net recognition errors. DifficultyScore=4 is appropriate despite being conceptual because the conceptual distinction is subtle and the distractors are sophisticated.

must_have.criterion: Requires interpreting exhibits or financial statements embedded in the stem
must_have.rationale: Items where the candidate must extract data from an exhibit before performing a calculation test integrated reasoning — a hallmark of Difficult CMA items. The exhibit adds a cognitive decode step before the calculation begins.
must_have.notes: Most stand-alone MCQ items do not have embedded exhibits (exhibits are case-study features). This criterion primarily applies to case-study items, which already have better Difficult calibration (35.7% Difficult in case pool vs. 3.3% in MCQ pool). A small number of MCQ items embed mini-tables in the stem text.

must_have.rationale: Items that require simultaneous knowledge from two different topic areas (e.g., cash budget + learning curve, variance analysis + flexible budget, CVP + tax effects) demand cognitive integration beyond single-topic application. These items test the candidate's ability to synthesize — even if the individual operations are Apply-level, the synthesis component elevates difficulty.
must_have.examples: A cash budget item requiring both (a) collections forecasting from Section B AND (b) cost behavior analysis from Section D is a Difficult-level integration task.

must_have.criterion: Has proven to be difficult for candidates (analytics-backed)
must_have.rationale: If historical analytics data exists showing an item's correct-answer rate below 50% among prepared candidates, it is empirically Difficult regardless of surface characteristics. However, no learner analytics data currently exists in this repository (all CorrectPercentage fields are unpopulated). This criterion is forward-looking — once analytics are active, it will be the most reliable recalibration signal.
must_have.current_status: Not applicable — no analytics data exists. All recalibration must rely on structural analysis (criteria C1-C5).

exclusion_criteria.criterion: DL-031 pattern: stem is a textbook definition and correct answer is the term being defined
exclusion_criteria.action: Recalibrate DOWNWARD (Moderate→Easy or Moderate-Easy), never upward
exclusion_criteria.rationale: Agent F confirmed 12 of 38 Domain E seeds (31.6%) follow DL-031. Agent C estimated ~500 pool-wide. These items should be Easy(1), not Moderate(3) or Difficult(4). Recalibrating DL-031 items upward compounds the inflation error.

exclusion_criteria.criterion: CognitiveLevel is Remember or Understand in Sections E or F
exclusion_criteria.action: Recalibrate DOWNWARD only — these are definitional/conceptual items mislabeled as Moderate
exclusion_criteria.rationale: Sections E (COSO, governance, ethics) and F (technology, ERP, analytics) are predominantly conceptual. The cognitive ceiling for most Section E/F items is Understand. Labeling them Moderate(3) is inflation; labeling them Difficult(4) would be double inflation.

exclusion_criteria.action: Remain Moderate(3) or move to Moderate-Easy(2)
exclusion_criteria.rationale: A single arithmetic operation (e.g., break-even units = fixed costs / CM per unit) tests Apply but at a routinized level. These belong at Moderate(3) or Moderate-Easy(2), not Difficult(4). Pack B's benchmark has such items at Moderate(3) — e.g., most Section B budget-sequencing items.

exclusion_criteria.action: Review — likely a simple item mislabeled as Moderate. Not a Difficult candidate.
exclusion_criteria.rationale: Complex items require complex explanations. A very short EC text suggests the item is more straightforward than its Moderate label implies. These should be audited for DL-031 or single-step simplicity.

phase_1_targets.description: Phase 1 targets 15% Difficult per pack as an intermediate calibration goal. The full CAQS target is 25%, but reaching that requires authoring new content (Phase 2) — recalibrating existing items alone cannot close the full gap.
phase_1_targets.methodology: 15% target selected as the midpoint between current state (3.3% pool-wide) and CAQS target (25%). Reaching 15% requires ~296 recalibrations from Moderate→Difficult across all packs. This is achievable through recalibration alone without requiring new item authoring. The remaining 10% gap (15%→25%) requires Phase 2 content expansion.

selection_methodology.description: How to select which specific Moderate items to recalibrate to Difficult within each pack and section
selection_methodology.step_1: Filter by section: limit to Sections A, B, C, D only. Exclude Sections E and F entirely — per Agent C F-C06, Agent F domain analysis, and DL-031 concentration in conceptual domains.
selection_methodology.step_2: Filter by cognitive demand: require CognitiveLevel === 'Apply'. Pool-wide, only ~1,200 items are Apply-level. Of the ~900 Moderate items in Sections A-D, approximately 550-650 are Apply. This is the candidate pool.
selection_methodology.step_3: Filter by calculation: require CalculationItem === true OR stem contains multi-part business scenario (>150 characters). Exclude single-sentence definitional stems (DL-031 pattern).
selection_methodology.step_4: Filter by explanation complexity: require ExplanationCorrect.length > 200 characters. Complex items have complex explanations. Short EC text indicates a conceptually simple item.
selection_methodology.step_5: Prioritize by distractor sophistication: prefer items where at least 2 of 3 distractor ExplanationWrong fields are >= 100 characters with choice-specific text. Boilerplate 'does not align with...' text suggests the distractors are not engineered for difficulty.
selection_methodology.step_6: Section B first, then C, then D, then A. Within each section, prioritize items with higher Topic sequence numbers (later in the section = generally more advanced concepts within the rotation group pattern).
selection_methodology.step_7: Exclude items with open structural defects: DL-008, DL-026, DL-013 (full boilerplate). Difficulty recalibration should not be performed on items with known content defects — fix the defect first, then recalibrate.

risks.description: Recalibration without per-item review may label items as Difficult that do not warrant it
risks.impact: HIGH — learners encounter items labeled Difficult that feel Moderate, reducing trust in the simulator's difficulty calibration
risks.mitigation: Every recalibrated item must pass per-item review verifying it meets at least criteria C1 AND C2 (calculation with Apply level in Sections A-D). Batch size ≤30 per governance-guard Rule 5. Pre-recalibration backup mandatory. Recalibrated items should be independently spot-checked at 20% sampling rate.

risks.description: Difficulty label alone does not change the item's actual cognitive demand
risks.impact: MEDIUM — relabeling an Apply-level single-step calculation from Moderate(3) to Difficult(4) makes the distribution look better on paper but does not prepare learners for genuinely Difficult CMA exam items
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 recalibration should target the genuinely most demanding items using the multi-step calculation filter (C1). Items meeting only 'borderline' criteria should be deferred to Phase 2 content enhancement (add a calculation step, not just a label change). The criteria are intentionally strict to avoid label inflation.

risks.description: Pack E may lack enough Apply items in Sections A-D to reach its 59-item target
risks.impact: MEDIUM — Pack E's 77% Understand skew means the candidate pool may be 40-50 items, not 59. Forcing recalibration on Understand-level items would produce fraudulent Difficult labels.
risks.mitigation: Accept a lower Phase 1 target for Pack E (e.g., 12% Difficult = 65 items → 43 recalibrations) if the candidate pool proves insufficient. The shortfall transfers to Phase 2 content expansion. Do not force recalibration on Understand-level items.

risks.description: DL-016 (metadata-content block misalignment) may cause scan tools to misidentify Moderate items that are structurally non-Moderate
risks.impact: MEDIUM — items where metadata-block Difficulty differs from what the renderer uses would be missed or incorrectly targeted
risks.mitigation: For Packs A/C/D (dual-block architecture), read DifficultyScore from the content block (where Stem/Choices live), not from the metadata block. Per AGENTS.md §5: cross-check any scan claims against raw file/line evidence.

risks.description: Existing 85 Difficult items may themselves be inflated and should not serve as recalibration benchmarks
risks.impact: LOW — if current Difficult items are incorrectly labeled, they model the wrong standard for new Difficult items
risks.mitigation: Agent F's S810.1 analysis of Domain E/D seeds found all 10 'Difficult'-labeled items were overstated. Before using Pack B items as benchmarks, audit 10% of existing Difficult items across all packs for label accuracy. P1E-E-037 was a confirmed DL-030 error. If the audit finds >20% inflation, existing Difficult items should be recalibrated downward in a separate corrective pass, not used as calibration targets.

risks.description: Sections E and F Moderate items need DOWNWARD recalibration (DL-031), which may affect Phase 1 Moderate→Difficult targets
risks.impact: LOW — downward recalibration of ~200 Section E/F Moderate items to Easy/Moderate-Easy reduces the Moderate pool, but the Phase 1 calculations already exclude Sections E and F. The remaining Moderate→Difficult pool in Sections A-D is unaffected.
risks.mitigation: Run the DL-031 downward recalibration in parallel (Agent G's scope). The two recalibration directions do not intersect — they operate on disjoint sections.

phase_2.description: Author new Difficult and Very Difficult items through content expansion to bridge the remaining gap from 15% to 25% Difficult and 0% to 10% Very Difficult
phase_2.estimated_effort: ~254 new Difficult items + ~254 new Very Difficult items = ~508 new items. At current certification pipeline capacity (~200 items per wave), this requires 3-4 certification waves across 8-12 sessions.
phase_2.target_sections: Prioritize Sections B and C (highest calculation density, largest absolute gaps). Then Sections A and D. Sections E and F need content that goes beyond definitions (e.g., fraud investigation scenarios for Section E, data analytics interpretation for Section F).
phase_2.leverage_case_study_pool: The case study pool has 266 Difficult items (35.7%) — study these items for templates of what Difficult calibration looks like. The case study scenarios (multi-exhibit, integrated) naturally produce Difficult-caliber cognitive demand.
phase_2.blocked_by: Phase 2 requires the authoring pipeline to be active (not currently operational). No launch date committed.

section_b_priority.why_highest_priority: Largest section (500 items), most calculation-intensive domain, largest absolute Difficult gap (108 items short of 25% target). The real CMA Part 1 exam has Section B items that require multi-step budget preparation, learning curve applications, and cash forecasting with borrowing constraints — all of which are naturally Difficult-level tasks.
specific_item_types_to_target: Learning curve: cumulative average time calculations with 3+ doublings (like P1B-B-200 benchmark)
Cash budget with borrowing: multi-step collections + disbursements + minimum balance constraint
Flexible budget + variance reconciliation: integrated analysis across 2+ variance types
Master budget sequencing: multi-department budget dependencies (not 'which comes first?' — that is DL-031 definition-match)
Sensitivity analysis: what-if scenarios requiring recalculation under changed assumptions

section_c_priority.why_second_highest: Performance management items test variance analysis, ROI/RI, balanced scorecard, transfer pricing — all require multi-step calculations with judgment. Same item count and same delta as Section B (500 items, 108 Difficult short).
specific_item_types_to_target: Four-variance analysis (spending + efficiency + budget + volume) — requires understanding all 4 components simultaneously
ROI vs. RI comparison with investment base changes — dual-metric analysis
Transfer pricing with capacity constraints — multi-party optimization
Flexible budget performance report: actual vs. flexible budget vs. master budget reconciliation

sections_a_d.priority: Third tier. Sections A (375 items) and D (375 items) require calculation proficiency but have fewer items. Combined 162 Difficult target. Calculation-heavy topics (cash flow indirect method, process costing with equivalent units, joint cost allocation with NRV) are natural Difficult candidates.
sections_a_d.constraint: Pack A Section A has zero Difficult items — the worst per-section calibration in the pool. Even reaching 15% (11 items) is a significant upgrade. Pack D Section D has DL-012 clone artifacts that reduce unique candidates.

sections_e_f.priority: NOT candidates for upward recalibration. These sections are predominantly conceptual. Agent F's S810.1 analysis of 38 Domain E seeds found 60.5% overstated and 0% that justified Difficult. The existing 'Difficult' labels in Pack D Section E (10 items) are all inflated by 1-3 score points and should be recalibrated DOWNWARD.
sections_e_f.recommended_action: Run DL-031 downward recalibration on Sections E and F first. This will reduce the Moderate count and correct the Easy deficit simultaneously. Once the conceptual foundation is calibrated correctly, Phase 2 content expansion can add genuinely Difficult items (fraud investigation scenarios, data analytics interpretation tasks, COSO ERM multi-component assessments) that go beyond definition-matching.

conditions: 1. Per-item review required: no bulk recalibration without verifying each item against criteria C1-C6. Batch size ≤30 per governance-guard Rule 5.
2. Pack E target may need downward adjustment: if fewer than 59 Apply-level Moderate items in Sections A-D are found, accept 12% Difficult (65 items, 43 recalibrations) as an interim target.
3. Sections E and F excluded from upward recalibration entirely: zero Moderate→Difficult items from Sections E/F. Agent F evidence is dispositive.

4. Existing Difficult items must be audited before serving as benchmarks: 10% sample audit across all packs. If >20% inflation rate found, existing Difficult items require corrective recalibration first.
5. Pre-existing defects (DL-008, DL-026, DL-013) must be resolved on candidates before difficulty recalibration.
6. DifficultyScore must match Difficulty label: any label/score mismatch (e.g., label='Difficult' but score=2, found in 14 of 38 Agent F reviewed items) must be corrected in the same pass.
7. REVISION_HISTORY.md entry required: document every recalibration batch with before/after counts, list of QIDs, and governing criteria applied.

8. governance-guard.js must be updated to enforce Difficulty label ↔ DifficultyScore consistency (new Rule 7 or extension of existing rule). 36.8% of Domain E seeds had label/score mismatches — this is a systematic defect needing automated enforcement.
